answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to post a bond in a scarce, externally costly resource before it can trade or earn reputation. The protocol records the bond against a public key, then slashes it when an identity is proven to double-spend or collude under predefined rules. A cheap inlet for creating names is harmless if each name needs its own locked stake: the attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it, rather than multiplying influence for free. A cipher can protect private agent data, while the kernel enforces bond checks.
